corrections.source_says: The values 115, 32, 42, 41, and 65 count meta-analytic effect-size estimates. They do not count condition-level sets of outputs, which is the codebook definition of unit=set. Preserve these explicitly labeled effect-size counts in synthesis and reported descriptions; the number of output sets is not reported and should be null. The meta-analysis has no applicable output-unit category among the form choices.

confirmed: Source independently read: all 17 pages of PsyArXiv v2, DOI 10.31234/osf.io/9u2ke_v2, including all references and the accepted-manuscript notice on p. 17; no appended supplement. The PDF was read in memory from https://osf.io/download/dkw94/; Tables 2-3 were checked against PDF text and rendered images. OSF and Crossref confirm posting on 2025-07-01; the filename, title, authors, and page count match the form (OSF preprint/file API; PDF pp. 1 and 17).

Crossref confirms the ACM proceedings DOI 10.1145/3746175.3746189, publication date 2025-10-06, and pages 1-11; its PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 in this check. The recorded findings are supported by the explicitly identified preprint, without claiming verification against the ACM PDF (Crossref works API; https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3746175.3746189).

Design_class=synthesis, context_class=synthesis, and core=no are correct. This manuscript reports a meta-analysis, with no original randomized study assigning people to AI assistance; its included comparisons require separate human and prompted-GenAI idea generation without further interaction and exclude computational co-creativity (pp. 5-6, Sections 3 and 3.2).

There are 15 articles, 17 studies, and 115 effect sizes, with a search window of January 2022 to January 2025. No pooled count of people randomized or analyzed is reported; the null participant counts are appropriate, and the fewer-than-50-people rule does not classify this synthesis (p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 7, Section 3.4 and Table 1).

Effect sizes are extracted or calculated Cohen’s d, with one study calculated from its original dataset; positive values favor GenAI. The three-level model handles sampling variance, within-study variance, and between-study variance. The paper does not establish a common participant-level standardizer across the underlying studies (pp. 7-8, Sections 3.4-3.5).

S1-O1 and synthesis.pooled[0:2]: d=.360, 95% CI [-.071, .790], Q(df=114)=2516.39, p<.001; after removing 14 influential values, d=.236, 95% CI [-.073, .544], Q(df=100)=1661.00, p<.001. All match the PDF (p. 8, Section 4.1).
Construct counts match: usefulness has 32 effect sizes from 10 studies, originality 42 from 14, and creativity as a singular construct 41 from 7 (p. 9, Section 4.1).
S1-O2 and synthesis.pooled[2:4]: the usefulness reference intercept is .175 [-.286, .635], and .147 [-.189, .482] without influential values; intervals are 95% CIs (p. 9, Table 2).

S1-O3 and synthesis.pooled[4:6]: originality relative to usefulness is .323 [.040, .606], and .173 [-.081, .352] without influential values; moderation Qm(df=2)=5.03, p=.081, and Qm(df=2)=1.78, p=.410. The latter estimate and CI are reproduced exactly as printed (p. 9, Section 4.1 and Table 2).

S1-O4 and synthesis.pooled[6:8]: creativity relative to usefulness is .144 [-.161, .448], and .088 [-.176, .352] without influential values. These and the originality coefficients are differences from the usefulness reference, as the form states (p. 9, Table 2 and its note).

S1-O5 and synthesis.pooled[8:10]: ChatGPT has 65 effect sizes from 13 studies, d=.478, 95% CI [-.040, .996], Q(df=64)=1825.73, p<.001; after removing 2 influential values, d=.374, 95% CI [-.047, .975]. The sensitivity estimate and interval match the PDF exactly (p. 10, Section 4.2).

Table 3 values match S1-O5 and synthesis.pooled[10:16]: GPT-4 reference .554 [-.019, 1.128] and .439 [-.035, .914]; GPT-3.5 relative to GPT-4 -.220 [-.726, .286] and -.197 [-.635, .241]; GPT-3 relative to GPT-4 -.476 [-2.506, 1.554] and -.362 [-2.034, 1.309]. Each pair is complete data followed by data without influential values; moderation Qm(df=2)=.90, p=.637, and Qm(df=2)=.92, p=.631 (p. 10, Table 3 and note).

The stated human populations and task examples match Table 1 (p. 7); Section 4.2 confirms 14 distinct language models excluding model versions, plus DALL·E 2 (p. 10). No diversity or homogenization outcome is analyzed in this synthesis (pp. 6-10, inclusion criteria and analyses).

The one-line finding correctly reports the study/effect-size counts, pooled estimate, confidence interval, sensitivity estimate, and ChatGPT estimate; the principal intervals include zero (pp. 7-10, Sections 3.4 and 4.1-4.2).
The external supplement is identified at https://osf.io/2xdba/ and contains the systematic search material, dataset, and analysis script (p. 5, Section 3 and footnote 1; public OSF file listing).
summary: This paper is a synthesis with no randomized study of people receiving generative-AI assistance, and its study counts, reported statistics, and one-line finding match the 17-page PsyArXiv v2 accepted manuscript. Two coding corrections are needed: the pooled measures include automated originality scores, and the outcome counts denote effect sizes rather than sets of outputs.
